summary: Spring Butte's 1932 L-4 lookout was replaced by a 41-foot octagonal-cab pole tower in 1991 or 1992; a 2025 visitor report says staffing ended in 2024 (unconfirmed).

facts.design: 41-foot pole tower with 16 by 16 foot octagonal cab (replaced the 1932 tower, which had an L-4 cab)
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com describe the present tower without any closure. A 2025 visitor report on Cheryl Hill's page says it stopped being staffed after failing a September 2024 inspection; no other source read confirms this.

visit.trail_note: A June 2020 visitor found the gate open and drove to the top. No source read says whether the public may enter the cab.

events.note: First lookout on the site: a pole tower with an L-4 cab, reported at 28, 30 or 32 feet depending on the source.
A bolt struck near the lookout on May 27 and started a timber fire, checked by C. E. Hein, who was temporarily on duty.
Operated by the Walker Range Patrol, staffed for 180 days and reporting to LaPine by telephone.
Lightning-caused spot fire west of Paulina Peak, put out by lookout Gene Roberts and Dave Adrian.
Tower rebuilt using tamarack logs for the legs.
Determined unsafe and closed until further notice.
Original tower dismantled in September; parts inventoried and stored.
Present 41-foot pole tower with 16 by 16 foot octagonal cab. Register Built field and firelookout.com say 1992; the Register text and a Sun item quoted by Oregon Lookouts point to 1991.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on May 30, 1996.
Per a 2025 visitor report, staffing ended after a failed September 2024 inspection. Not confirmed by other sources read.

corrections.proposed: 41-foot pole tower with 16 by 16 foot octagonal cab
corrections.why: The L-4 cab belonged to the 1932 tower, which was dismantled in 1991. The Register and Cheryl Hill both describe the present tower's octagonal cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register Built field and firelookout.com give 1992. The Register text and a Sun item quoted by Oregon Lookouts point to a 1991 erection. Both years are kept in the events and story.
Oregon Lookouts gives 28, 30 and 32 feet for the same 1932 tower, quoting a 30-foot figure from the August 1932 Bend Bulletin item.

The 2020 visit and firelookout.com describe a staffed lookout. A single 2025 visitor report says staffing ended after a failed September 2024 inspection. That report is not confirmed by the other sources read, so staffing is recorded as disputed.

notes_for_editor: Two of four sources (firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill) agree on 1992 and the 41-foot tower. The Register's Built field and text disagree, and the record keeps both. The 2025 staffing report is only on Cheryl Hill's page and is not verified; that is the main open question. The brief's design L-4 describes the 1932 tower and is corrected. Access rules for the cab are not in any source read. firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Gary Weber but gives no image URLs, so no photos were added. The Register's Administered-by field was cut off in the fetch, so agency rests on firelookout.com and the Oregon Lookouts page.
